chunks: Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"Whoever performs wudu (ablution) and completes the wudu thoroughly, then begins the salat (prayer) and prays four rakʿahs, separating between them with a taslim, reciting in each rakʿah Fātiḥat al-Kitāb once and
fifty times, he will finish when he finishes, and there will remain no sin between him and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that He will forgive him."

key_terms.أَسْبَغَ ٱلْوُضُوءَ: completed the wudu thoroughly and properly
key_terms.بِتَسْلِيمَةٍ: with a salutation separating the sets of prayer
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ ٱلْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, the Opening of the Book

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing the four-rakʿah prayer with repeated recitation of Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a recommended salat performed with thorough wudu (ablution), four rakʿahs, and repeated recitation of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ. It emphasizes the spiritual merit of careful worship and promises divine forgiveness for the one who performs it as described.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1556 - Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"Whoever performs ablution and completes it thoroughly, then begins the prayer and prays four units (rak'ahs), separating each two with a taslim (salutation), and recites in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) once and
fifty times, he will finish his prayer with nothing between him and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, except that his sins will be forgiven."
